timing: retrospective specification of previously generated candidate

sourceFacts.fact: PAH catalyses conversion of phenylalanine to tyrosine.
Reduced PAH activity impairs this conversion and allows phenylalanine to accumulate.

clinicalSources.title: ACMG: Elevated phenylalanine newborn-screening ACT sheet

invariants: Both rows point phenylalanine to tyrosine.
Deficiency means reduced conversion, not universal total enzyme absence.
layoutSpecification: Two horizontal pathways, very clear hand-painted biochemistry diagram. Title 'Phenylalanine → tyrosine'. Upper heading 'Usual conversion': large teal rounded box 'Phenylalanine' on LEFT and ochre box 'Tyrosine' on RIGHT connected by a broad arrow pointing RIGHT, label ABOVE arrow 'Phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH)'. Lower heading 'PAH deficiency': same phenylalanine box with three small circles collecting underneath, same tyrosine box slightly faded; connecting rightward arrow has a small perpendicular bar interrupting it, label 'Reduced conversion'. Small bottom text 'Phenylalanine accumulates'. No molecular structures, no treatment doses, no implication of complete enzyme absence in every phenotype.
forbiddenAnatomy: No claimed anatomical reconstruction, diagnostic image, histology or literal neuroanatomical pathway
No organ cutaways or invented internal spatial relationships

validation.sourceFacts: Checked against listed primary clinical sources during original topic review
validation.pixelChecks: Visually inspected: both reaction arrows point from phenylalanine to tyrosine; PAH label identifies enzyme; deficiency row shows reduced conversion and phenylalanine accumulation. No reversed reaction, dosage or complete-deficiency claim.
